business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Massively Multiplayer Online Role-Playing Games

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of Panama (Private Interest Foundation regime under Law 25 of 1995)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Panamanian Civil Code and Code of Commerce), supplemented by Anglo-influenced private foundation and trust legislation
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States-Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA), in force since 31 October 2012, including investment chapter protections
Panama-Republic of Korea Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income, in force
Panama-United Arab Emirates Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income and Capital, in force
Double Taxation and Tax Information Exchange instruments entered into by the Republic of Panama under its network of tax agreements

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Ley de Fundaciones de Interés Privado); Decreto Ley 2 de 22 de febrero de 2011 (creation of the Unidad de Análisis Financiero and the Consejo Nacional contra el Blanqueo de Capitales); Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT framework and customer due diligence obligations); Ley 70 de 2019 as amended by Ley 129 de 2020 and regulated by Decreto Ejecutivo 137 de 2020 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales, administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos of the Ministry of Economy and Finance); Ley 38 de 2000 (Administrative Procedure Act). For the global digital publishing payment chain, the standardized beneficial ownership attribution threshold is applied at 25% in alignment with FATF Recommendation 24; Panamanian implementing regulations additionally require identification of natural persons holding 10% or more of the rights or equity of a legal vehicle, and for private interest foundations the Founder and identifiable vested Beneficiaries must be declared in the confidential UBO registry.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and registered Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación / Escritura Pública de Fundación de Interés Privado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Circuit of Panama and Registro Público de Panamá
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization depending on the jurisdiction of use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Internal Regulations of the Private Interest Foundation (Reglamento), including Foundation Council governance and beneficiary provisions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Circuit of Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Registration in the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Dirección General de Ingresos, Ministry of Economy and Finance of Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Tax Solvency Certificate (Certificado de Paz y Salvo)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Dirección General de Ingresos of Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Registered Office and Resident Agent appointment certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed resident agent and/or Registro Público de Panamá

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of the Founder, Foundation Council members, Protector and Beneficiaries against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK OFSI List, and the Panamanian UAF published list of persons linked to illicit activities; mandatory PEP identification and enhanced due diligence under Law 23 of 2015 covering family members and close associates; verification of source of funds and source of wealth for all contributors to the foundation; adverse media review and negative news check; ongoing transaction monitoring obligations of the resident agent and regulated service providers.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Departamento de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (official portal: https://www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official language of registry instruments is Spanish; however, the foundation name may be expressed in a foreign language provided it is written in Latin script. Names originating in non-Latin scripts (Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic, etc.) must be submitted in an officially transliterated Latin-script version certified by the applicant. The name must be visually and phonetically distinguishable from any existing registered entity, and standard practice requires the suffix 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or the abbreviation 'F.I.P.' for legal clarity in banking and payment-platform onboarding.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant or its licensed attorney may file a written reconsideration petition with the Registro Público de Panamá within ten working days of notification under Ley 38 de 2000; if denied, a hierarchical administrative appeal may be lodged with the Director General of the Registro Público, followed by judicial review before the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia. An alternative name variant may be submitted while the appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for statutory purposes when operated by a licensed resident agent providing mail-forwarding and service-of-process infrastructure; however, the MMORPG publishing and in-app purchase business profile requires demonstrable operational substance in Panama or at the place of effective management, including board minutes, books and records, commercial contracts, and economic decision-making documentation, in order to satisfy Apple App Store and Google Play payout KYC expectations and correspondent banking due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 5-10% annualized probability for a low-risk holding foundation confined to intellectual property ownership and payout management; probability rises to 20-30% if the foundation becomes the direct contracting entity with local employees, physical premises, or payment flows that trigger UAF or banking alerts.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Private Interest Foundation Law of Panama (Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995), as amended by Ley 12 de 2016; Article 7 (minimum initial endowment), Article 12 (foundation charter content), Article 19 (registration with the Public Registry); supplemental application of the General Law on Commercial Companies (Ley 32 de 1927) where not contrary to Law 25.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (notarized Foundation Charter)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum initial endowment of US$10,000 (or B/.10,000) in cash or in-kind assets prescribed by the Foundation Charter. No statutory bank escrow deposit is mandatory; the endowment is subscribed and allocated in the Charter and its due receipt must be acknowledged by the Foundation Council in the first resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial endowment of USD 10,000 recorded in the Foundation Charter is hereby accepted and credited to the foundation's capital; that the registered office shall be located at [address], managed by the appointed Resident Agent, P.H. [Agent], República de Panamá; that the Council is constituted and the following officers are appointed: [President], [Secretary], [Treasurer]; that the Council may open bank accounts, execute digital distribution agreements for MMORPG content, and instruct the Resident Agent to effect all Public Registry filings; that any Council member may sign individually for administrative acts; that this resolution takes effect immediately and shall be minuted in the Council book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage Resident Agent and Legal Counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: None (private contractual step before a licensed Panamanian lawyer)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a licensed attorney and an authorized resident agent (fiduciary company). Execute the resident agent engagement letter and obtain the agent's written consent to serve. Verify the proposed foundation name against the Public Registry's database and reserve a name if required by the chosen agent.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of founders and beneficiaries
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected by the Public Registry, promptly resubmit with an alternative approved name before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Foundation Charter before Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública (Notary Public of the Circuit where the foundation is formed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública) in Spanish, including foundation name, registered agent, initial endowment clause, purpose (ISIC 5820 MMORPG publishing), and Council composition. All founders appear before the notary to execute the deed, and the resident agent accepts its appointment.
required_dossiers: Initial endowment proof or commitment letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects formal defects, correct the deed and re-execute the instrument; re-notarization may be required before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized first copy (testimonio) of the Foundation Charter to the Public Registry together with the official fee payment. The Registry reviews compliance with Law 25 and issues the inscribed foundation certificate (inscripción).
required_dossiers: Legal counsel's certification of due execution
Notarized power of attorney of the filing representative (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect notice (mandamiento), the legal counsel must submit corrected pages or a clarifying brief within five business days; a re-notarized document is required only if the Registry orders it.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Identification Number (RUC) and Municipal Operating Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Alcaldía o Municipio de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the inscribed foundation certificate, register the foundation for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) at the DGI. Subsequently apply for the municipal business operations notice (Aviso de Operación) at the municipality where the physical office or virtual business seat is located.
required_dossiers: Passport of the registered agent and officers
Proof of office address (rental contract or utility invoice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI or the municipality rejects incomplete documentation, remedy the deficiency within ten business days; for zoning objections, obtain a zoning certificate or submit an alternative office address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt First Foundation Council Resolution and Open Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council / Licensed Resident Agent; Panamanian banking institution (AML/KYC compliance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a formal meeting of the Foundation Council to adopt the first resolution accepting the initial endowment, appointing officers, and authorizing the opening of corporate bank accounts. File the signed resolution in the Foundation's minute book and provide a notarized excerpt to the bank for account opening.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's KYC unit requests additional source-of-funds documentation, deliver the requested evidence immediately; if the account application is denied despite compliance, consider a secondary licensed bank with a fintech-friendly onboarding process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Operational Clearance (Fire Safety and Workplace License)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For any physical office or co-working workspace, apply for a fire safety inspection certificate and, if the entity becomes an employer with up to 20 workers, register the workplace with MITRADEL. The permits are renewed annually.
required_dossiers: Proof of premises ownership or lease
Fire extinguisher and alarm maintenance records
Registry of employees or payroll roster
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection reports deficiencies, correct the hazards (exit signs, extinguishers, wiring) and request a re-inspection within fifteen days; similar remediation applies for MITRADEL compliance orders.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 5820 (software publishing / MMORPG); if the company later establishes physical manufacturing, server hardware assembly, or distribution logistics, the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) would become the competent industrial licensing authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Aviso de Operación (Business Operation Notice) is the only mandatory operating permit for a Panamanian office; no sectoral authorization or statutory publishing license is required for MMORPG digital content.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III – Exempt / Registration only; non-industrial office and software-related activities do not require a full EIA study, and only a simple environmental registration is obtained if the entity occupies a permanent office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluents are permitted. Wastewater discharged to public sewerage must comply with IDAAN/ANAM limits of BOD5 below 350 mg/L, COD below 700 mg/L, pH 6–9, and TSS below 350 mg/L; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from cleaning solvents in office operations are negligible and must not exceed 50 ppm except for temporary maintenance. Electronic waste (servers, screens, batteries) must be handled by authorized recyclers per Resolution AG-0420-2017.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (Plan de Seguridad Contra Incendios), municipal structural load inspection when workspace exceeds 200 m², and workplace health clearance from the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) for any payroll employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Directorate of Revenues (Dirección General de Ingresos – DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), Panama; online taxpayer portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is incorporated under Law 25 of 1995 and registered in the Public Registry through a Panamanian registered agent. After incorporation, the PIF must obtain its single taxpayer identification number (RUC) from the DGI by filing the DGI registration application, the notarized foundation charter and bylaws, the Public Registry certificate, identification of the founding council members and resident agent, and the notified Panamanian address. Non-resident founders and beneficiaries are permitted and may remain confidential. Once verified, the DGI issues a permanent RUC, which also integrates the foundation into the ITBMS taxpayer registry where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope – The PIF is a separate legal person subject to entity-level taxation only on Panama-source income; foreign-source income, including revenue from offshore digital game publishing and in-app purchases collected through Apple/Google payouts, is not within Panama's income tax net. Economic activities performed in Panama, such as local support, local server deployment, or local monetization, will trigger normal Panama-source entity-level taxation and ITBMS compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a US-style check-the-box election, pass-through election, or hybrid mismatch classification election for Private Interest Foundations. Tax classification follows the territorial-source rules of the Panama Fiscal Code and Law 25 of 1995. A PIF may elect its internal governance provisions under Law 25, and may voluntarily register for ITBMS where below the small-taxpayer threshold, but no elective pass-through or hybrid branch classification is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) – Panama's value-added tax equivalent (VAT/GST).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All legal entities carrying out taxable acts in Panama are required to register for ITBMS regardless of turnover. Panama maintains a small-taxpayer simplified regime for annual gross taxable turnover up to B/.36,000 (approximately US$36,000); businesses above that threshold are mandatory ITBMS-registered. For digital service suppliers, including MMORPG platform operators, Panamanian nexus arises from sales of electronically supplied services to consumers located in Panama, and registration under Law 20 of 2019 may apply from the first transaction without a de minimis threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama has phased in mandatory electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica) through the DGI's Sede Electrónica platform. Registered taxpayers subject to the electronic-invoicing schedule must issue invoices using DGI-authorized software or qualified cloud/API service providers, transmit invoice datasets to the DGI in real time or immediately upon issuance, and include a DGI authorization code and QR code on each valid invoice. Manual invoices are not allowed for taxpayers in the mandatory electronic-invoicing regime for purposes of ITBMS credits, export substantiation, or refund claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated for ITBMS where title and possession pass to a non-Panama buyer and the goods physically depart Panama under a valid customs export declaration. For services, including offshore digital MMORPG subscription and in-app purchase revenues, zero-rating or non-taxability requires that the service is rendered to a non-resident recipient, is effectively used and enjoyed outside Panama, and is not attributable to a Panamanian business establishment. Platform settlement records from Apple App Store and Google Play should identify the non-Panama platform operator and non-Panama end-consumer pool. Income tax benefits under the territorial system likewise require that the economic activity be performed abroad and, for export-of-goods cases, that export proceeds be repatriated to Panama within 180 days.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUSCA or equivalent Panamanian customs exit document)
Bill of Lading or airway bill evidencing physical exportation from Panama
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/FX statement proving repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days
Commercial invoice and sale contract with the non-Panama buyer
Platform revenue statements and payout records from Apple App Store and Google Play where services are exported digitally
RUC and ITBMS registration certificates and, if applicable, the DGI electronic invoice authorization refs for export invoices
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI audits export-related zero-rating claims by matching customs exit declarations, bills of lading, platform payment flows, bank transfers, and inward remittance certificates. If documentation is incomplete, contradictory, or the transaction is recharacterized as a Panamanian domestic supply, the DGI will assess ITBMS at 7% on the full invoice value, deny or claw back any refund previously granted, and charge monthly moratory interest plus administrative surcharges. Willful or fraudulent use of forged export documents, fictitious buyers, or false remittance certificates can trigger penalties of up to 100% of the omitted tax, criminal tax-fraud proceedings under Panamanian criminal tax law and Law 8 of 2010, and reopening of prior periods within the applicable five-year statute of limitations. Where the export qualification fails, the income may also be recharacterized as Panama-source and exposed to 25% corporate income tax.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama does not have an independent central bank. The US Dollar is constitutional legal tender under Decreto Ley 9 of 1998 regime, and monetary policy is effectively conducted by the US Federal Reserve through full dollarization. Banking supervision and licensing are exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP). The state-owned Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as the fiscal agent of the central government and provides lender-of-last-resort services, while Panama's coin-only national currency, the Balboa (PAB), circulates at an absolute fixed 1:1 parity with USD and has no independent monetary issuance or exchange rate mechanism.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama maintains unrestricted capital and current account convertibility. There is no legal distinction between capital and current account transactions; no exchange control law, no approval requirement, and no surrender obligation apply to residents or non-residents. The territorial taxation system and absence of exchange controls permit unconditional profit remittance, dividend distribution, and repatriation of foundation capital and earnings to any foreign beneficiary. No withholding tax is imposed on outbound distributions by a non-operating Panamanian Private Interest Foundation under Ley 25 de 1995, provided the foundation does not engage in Panamanian-sourced trade or business activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory timeline for the repatriation of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to channel export receipts through the domestic banking system. Digital service revenues, including Apple App Store and Google Play net settlements for MMORPG in-app purchases, are treated as exported services for territorial tax purposes and may be retained in any foreign financial institution or cleared through any correspondent channel. The only administrative obligation is the maintenance of accurate accounting records supporting the Panamanian-sourced versus foreign-sourced classification of income for the annual tax return (Declaración de Renta).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low immediate viability. Foreign electronic money institutions (EMIs) domiciled in the UK, EU, or Caribbean do not hold a Panamanian banking license and cannot directly provide a local USD account settlement rail that is recognized by Panamanian tax or banking authorities. Panama's SBP maintains an Innovation Hub (Módulo de Innovación Financiera) under Acuerdo 3 of 2023, but no comprehensive EMI licensing regime for digital payment institutions has been operationalized as of the current stage. A PIF is therefore advised to use regulated Panamanian commercial banks as the primary settlement gateway and may engage foreign EMIs only as auxiliary collection channels for global in-app purchase proceeds, provided the ultimate concentration account is held with an SBP-supervised bank. The 2022 Ley 21 crypto-asset authorization was partially declared unconstitutional by the Panamanian Supreme Court and offers no safe harbor for treasury clearing operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in-person or live video-verified interview with the compliance officer is required at the discretion of each bank. SBP Rule 8-2000 (Due Diligence) requires banks to identify the natural persons behind the client. In practice, Tier 1 Panamanian banks demand at least one physical visit by the foundation council member (Consejo de la Fundación) or the authorized signatory for the initial onboarding interview, after which the final interview may be conducted remotely through a notarized video conference or an apostilled power of attorney executed before a Panamanian notary. The foundation founder (Fundador) need not appear if a validly appointed foundation council member or Protector/Compliance Officer is present. All documents from foreign jurisdictions must be legalized by apostille (Hague Convention, of which Panama is a party) and translated into Spanish by a certified translator when required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque foundation structure: the Private Interest Foundation has no registered shareholders or equity registry, creating a beneficiary uncertainty red flag under SBP Rule 8-2000.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) certified copy of the Foundation Charter (Carta Fundacional) and Regulations (Reglamento) duly registered in the Registro Público de Panamá; (ii) registrar certificate of registration with date and folio number; (iii) formal council resolution appointing the authorized signatory; (iv) Supreme Decree-compliant beneficial ownership disclosure form identifying the founder, council members, and all named and prospective beneficiaries; and (v) legal opinion from a licensed Panamanian counsel confirming that the foundation is not a trust and that the council has no uncontrolled beneficiary discretion, supported by the defined-objective clause consistent with Ley 25 de 1995.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual revenue source for a Panamanian foundation: digital gaming and in-app purchases from Apple App Store and Google Play may be misclassified by the bank's AML department as gambling-related or anonymous virtual asset flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit (i) copies of the Apple Developer Program Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement showing the entity as the registered merchant; (ii) recent Apple and Google net settlement statements including transaction summaries and withholding tax reports (where applicable); (iii) read-only access or exported dashboard reports from App Store Connect and Google Play Console demonstrating itemized in-app purchase volume; (iv) audited or reconciled accounting ledger matching platform payouts to bank deposits; (v) a game description and published app store listing confirming MMORPG gameplay and absence of gambling features; and (vi) a brief legal memorandum classifying in-app purchases as standard digital services revenue exempt from Panamanian territorial tax.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Presumed lack of economic substance: the foundation may be flagged as a shell entity with no employees, office, or activity beyond passive holding of bank balances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) registered agent certificate issued by a licensed Panamanian law firm or licensed agent, confirming the registered office address; (ii) municipal operating license (Aviso de Operación) for the registered establishment; (iii) foundation council meeting minutes under seal showing treasury and operational decision-making; (iv) an economic substance summary demonstrating active contract management with Apple, Google, and payment processors; (v) service agreements with a Panamanian corporate administrator or back-office provider; and (vi) a shareholder-and-officer-free legal structure note showing that the foundation is a separate legal person created by law rather than an artificial shell.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Global player-base cross-border flows: incoming wires from Brazil, India, Turkey, or other high-volume MMORPG markets may trigger sanctions or source-of-funds reviews due to fragmented origins.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain (i) a sanctions screening protocol evidencing no connection to OFAC, EU, or UN sanctioned persons or countries; (ii) an aggregated settlement note showing that all inbound wires originate from Apple Distribution International, Google Payment Corp., or authorized local distributors, not from individual players; (iii) a flow diagram from player payment through Apple/Google merchant account to the Panamanian PIF treasury account; (iv) a country-of-player-access matrix extracted from app store analytics to substantiate the international nature of the business; and (v) a sworn auditor's confirmation that no direct peer-to-peer or gambling-related transfers enter the corporate account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the PIF's minimum capital requirement and the actual inflow profile: large streaming balances versus zero paid-in capital evidence may create a mismatch red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contribute the statutory minimum endowment (market practice USD 10,000 or as stated in the Foundation Charter) and deliver (i) a notarized contribution letter from the founder; (ii) the bank credit memo of the endowment deposit; (iii) the foundation charter reflecting the initial endowment as a schedule; and (iv) a notarized statement that subsequent balances are exclusively operating revenues from app store settlements, with supporting quarterly financial statements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire routing for the initial endowment and subsequent capital contributions: (1) identify the beneficiary account by the exact foundation name as registered in Panama, the bank's SWIFT BIC, the USD account number, and the foundation's registered address; (2) remit via SWIFT MT103 from the sending bank; (3) include in field 70 the narrative 'Initial endowment contribution to Private Interest Foundation under Ley 25 de 1995' or 'Capital contribution – software publishing entity PA_PIF'; (4) Panama does not use IBAN, but the beneficiary bank's U.S. correspondent address (typically a U.S. Fed-wire-agented institution such as Wells Fargo, JPMorgan Chase, or Citibank) must be listed for a USD clearing; (5) obtain a pre-notification letter from the foundation's council confirming the expected amount, sender, and purpose to the bank's compliance department; (6) the initial endowment is not taxable as income under the Panamanian territorial system and must be recorded as a capital surplus entry in the foundation's books; (7) Apple and Google remittances arrive as separate MT103 credits from App Store and Google distribution entities, which must be matched daily against platform settlement conversion reports.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade and operational settlement: (1) cross-border supplier payments for development, cloud hosting, marketing, and localized customer support are executed via SWIFT MT103 in USD, with each instruction carrying the exact foundation name, the beneficiary's full account data, and a commercially precise remittance narrative such as 'Licensed software development services' or 'Cloud infrastructure fees'; (2) commercial letters of credit (LC) for larger licensing or co-publishing commitments are issued through Banistmo or Banco General using the UCP 600 framework, advised by MT700/MT710, with proceeds settling via MT750/MT756; (3) local Panamanian disbursements are cleared through the Automated Clearing House of Panama (ACH Panama) operated by the Cámara Compensadora Automatizada, using the ABA equivalent, the domestic routing code, and the beneficiary's local account; (4) for intra-group transfers from the PIF to a foreign operating subsidiary or to the founder, only fixed-balance wire transfers with complete auditable trail are permitted, and the controller must record a formal council resolution authorizing each distribution under Ley 25 de 1995; (5) outbound USD wires clearing through the U.S. correspondent banking network require compliance with OFAC and the USA PATRIOT Act record retention, so the foundation must preserve full wire-support documentation for a minimum of five years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD is the foundation's functional and reporting currency; the gold-plated treasury regulation of Panama allows the PIF to open foreign currency accounts (EUR, GBP, CNY) in domestic banks for operational payouts to foreign developers; FX risks from foreign-currency denominated trade liabilities may be hedged with plain vanilla deliverable forward contracts negotiated under a bilateral ISDA Master Agreement with any SBP-licensed commercial bank, booked under the foundation's ISDA Schedule and Credit Support Annex.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging market currencies without active offshore deliverable markets (e.g., Brazilian real BRL, Argentine peso ARS, Turkish lira TRY, Indian rupee INR, Egyptian pound EGP) may be transacted offshore with international banks through a Panamanian bank's offshore trading desk or directly with a foreign counterparty, provided the transaction is documented under a Panamanian law-governed confirmation and the resulting non-deliverable settlement in USD is booked in the foundation's treasury ledger.

Permissible cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR and USD/GBP) for syndicated licensing or joint venture funding are authorized only for genuine economic hedge purposes, with mirror recognition in the foundation's accounting records under IAS/IFRS hedge accounting rules, and subject to a council-approved treasury policy limiting counterparty concentration to notional amounts below the registered banking group's lending ceiling; Panama's lack of a central bank imposes no stamp duty or regulatory approval on derivative contracts, and the SBP is not a hedging transaction counterparty.

For operational exposure from the Apple and Google payout cycles, the foundation may enter into short-term rolling forwards of up to 90 days to cover guaranteed future platform settlement commitments denominated in EUR, GBP, or JPY, provided the notional netting is calculated from the net settlement schedules of Apple App Store and Google Play and each forward is mirrored by a matched treasury record; options, exotic structures, and speculative positions are prohibited under the model treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax Payment (Impuesto Anual de Franquicia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, remittable through the Portal de Franquicias or authorized Panamanian banks
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment due annually no later than June 30 for the current calendar year, within the January 1 – June 30 payment window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a B/. 50 (USD 50) surcharge; failure to pay for two consecutive annual periods permits the Public Registry to dissolve the foundation administratively (strike-off), terminating juridical personality; reinstatement requires full settlement of arrears, surcharges and fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Annual Confirmation Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Final Beneficial Owner Electronic Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation due by March 31; any UBO change must be reported within 90 days of occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Law 70 of 2019 fines of B/. 5,000 to B/. 50,000 (approx. USD 5,000 to USD 50,000) for non-filing, late filing or knowingly false UBO data; registry certifications may be denied while the declaration remains outstanding.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Notarized Registration of Foundation Charter Amendments and Council Resolutions (for beneficiary substitutions, protector changes or council member changes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile Section, following notarial protocolization
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Immediately after adoption by the Foundation Council; registration must precede any reliance on the change against third parties
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unregistered resolutions are unenforceable against third parties and may trigger refusal of banking, payout-rail or transfer-agent services; delayed registration attracts additional notarial and Registry tariff surcharges.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No independent audit is statutorily required for a Private Interest Foundation limited to passive IP holding and foreign-source MMORPG publishing income. Mandatory certified audit attaches only where the foundation (i) generates Panamanian-source gross income within the DGI 'Gran Contribuyente' classification (commonly the DGI threshold range of B/. 750,000 – B/. 1,000,000 in annual taxable gross revenue); (ii) is licensed by a Panamanian regulator; or (iii) is expressly ordered by the DGI. Foreign digital-platform royalties fall outside Panama's territorial tax base and do not trigger the audit mandate.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Normas de Información Financiera de Panamá (NIF PAN), which are IFRS-based; the IFRS-for-SMEs edition applies for non-public-interest foundations. Internal accounting records may be kept in English, while any instrument protocolized before the Public Registry must be in Spanish. Accounting records and supporting contracts must be retained for a minimum of seven (7) years.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Foundation Council must maintain an up-to-date internal register identifying the founder, council members, any protector, and each natural person with ultimate beneficial control (generally persons entitled to 10% or more of foundation assets or distributions). Any transfer-like substitution of beneficiaries, change of council members, or charter modification must be adopted by notarized council resolution, reflected in the foundation instrument, and declared to the DGI UBO registry within 90 days; the annual electronic confirmation is due each March 31. The registered agent performs an annual KYC interview to validate the declaration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Final Beneficiaries and Protector Appointments
Foundation Minute Book and Charter Amendment Records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No audit fee expected under a purely territorial foreign-source structure; if voluntarily commissioned for financing or investor due diligence, USD 2,500 – USD 6,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat headline rate (Law 70 of 2019; progressive application: 15% on the first USD/PAB 50,000 of net taxable income and 25% on the excess above USD/PAB 50,000).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation excludes foreign-source income (0% Panama corporate income tax); the export-services regime under Fiscal Code Article 723-A renders eligible digital services delivered abroad effectively tax-neutral (0%-5%); the preferential 15% band applies on the first USD/PAB 50,000; dividends distributed from Panama-source taxed profit carry a 5% distribution tax; no Panama VAT/GST on digital exports.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 300 (Declaración Jurada Anual de Renta - Personas Jurídicas) filed through the DGI/General Directorate of Revenue eTax platform (eTax 2.0, MEF/DGI web portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Form 300); quarterly ancillary declarations for advance payments (Forms 400/401/402) and monthly retention returns. Fiscal year defaults to 1 January - 31 December for a newly incorporated PIF; other fiscal periods require prior DGI authorization.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the close of the fiscal period (31 March for a calendar-year PIF). Quarterly advance payments are due within 15 days after each quarter end; the DGI alert system flags any overdue Form 300 automatically.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC number, legal name, foundation charter registration, fiscal period (DD/MM/YYYY), audit-practice code, local address and electronic contact.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Panama resident legal representative (the Foundation Council or its appointed fiscal agent) with a local address; non-resident beneficiaries are not listed on the form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1 - Ingresos gravables de fuente panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from goods and services with Panama source: domestic in-app purchase revenue from Panamanian users, local subscriptions, and virtual currency sales to Panama cardholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Segregate by platform payout report; any transaction attributed to a Panamanian payor, billing address, or residential IP address is taxable at 15%/25%. Retain Apple/Google Store country reports as the evidential basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 - Ingresos exentos y no gravables (foreign-source income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All payout revenue from Apple App Store and Google Play for stores where the payer is domiciled abroad and games are consumed abroad; 0% under the territorial rule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a granular country-by-country revenue schedule and, where the Fiscal Code Article 723-A export-services regime is invoked, a sworn compliance declaration; keep Apple/Google payout extracts and platform statements for at least 7 years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct server costs, platform commissions, engine royalties, user-acquisition spend, payroll, amortization of game IP and administrative costs that are necessary and proportionate to the Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate expenses between Panama-source and foreign-source booklets on a consistent, documented basis; intercompany commission and royalty payments to related parties must be supported by a transfer pricing study when the related-party transaction exceeds USD/PAB 1.5 million.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions; apply the progressive table: first USD/PAB 50,000 at 15%, the excess at 25%. Loss offsets are limited to five years carried forward under Law 70 of 2019.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the Panama PIF, the net taxable base cannot be reduced by distributions, gratuities, or beneficiary payments; such arrangements are reclassified and taxed in the dividend withholding annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 23 - Impuesto a pagar o saldo a favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final liability after advance payments (Forms 400/401/402), third-party withholdings and tax credits; settlement requires an eTax payment slip (constancia de pago) generated within the declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay in USD/PAB from a Panamanian bank account or via bank transfer to DGI collection codes; non-resident filers without a Panama permanent establishment must still maintain a local fiscal agent; a 0% taxable result still requires proof of timely filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 300: surcharge of 10% of the tax due per month or fraction (maximum 100%); late-payment interest at the DGI official rate (circa 10% per annum); statutory fine for failure to file annexes (Forms 311, CRS/BO and ESR schedules) up to USD/PAB 1,000 per schedule; when no tax is due, the DGI applies a fixed administrative fine of USD/PAB 100-500 and blocks issuance of tax clearance; persistent default triggers strike-off proceedings and loss of legal standing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions to non-resident beneficiaries out of foreign-source income (territorial rule); 5% dividend distribution tax on distributions made from Panama-source net taxable profits (Fiscal Code Article 730); 10% charge on distribution of foreign-source profits to Panamanian resident beneficiaries (Fiscal Code Article 733). The charge is borne by the beneficiary and withholdable at the foundation level; Panama does not impose a general dividend withholding tax on non-resident shareholders beyond these cases.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For a Panama-resident PIF generating cross-border flows to treaty-protected beneficiaries (e.g., DTAs with the UK, Spain, Mexico, Netherlands, Ireland, Italy, South Korea, Singapore, Luxembourg, India, UAE, Barbados): the beneficiary must file a Panama Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) application through the DGI eTax portal (Form 305 / Certificado de Residencia Fiscal), attaching the prior-period Form 300, foundation charter, Council meeting minutes, and substance documents. The DGI issues the certificate in 10-15 business days for a fee of approximately USD/PAB 60. The certificate supports the beneficiary's domestic exemption or rate reduction claim in the payer's jurisdiction. For outbound distributions from Panama, no DGI treaty-clearance protocol is required because Panama imposes 0% WHT on foreign-source distributions; the TRC instead evidences non-resident status and triggers the 0%, 5%, or 10% rules above.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Panama statutory WHT on royalties paid to a non-resident for the use of IP within Panama: 12.5% (Law 70 of 2019, Fiscal Code Article 731); interest paid to non-resident creditors on loans executed and serviced abroad: 0% under territorial rules; interest on locally issued securities paid to non-residents: 12.5%; treaty protocols generally reduce royalties to 10% (e.g., UK, Ireland, UAE) and retain interest at 0% or 5%; dividends are typically 5%-15%. A non-resident licensor or lender should file a non-resident income tax return to claim any refund or treaty protection.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File, plus the annual related-party return (Form 311), when the aggregate value of related-party transactions equals or exceeds USD/PAB 1,500,000 in the fiscal year; taxpayers with transactions above USD/PAB 250,000 must maintain contemporaneous TP documentation available upon inspection (Fiscal Code Article 51F; Resolution 201-3942 of 2011). The threshold applies at the Panama legal person level, meaning the PIF or its permanent establishment.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance regime (Law 129 of 2019; Executive Decree 80 of 2020) applies to all Panamanian legal persons, including Private Interest Foundations engaged in commercial activity. A global MMORPG publisher/IP holder is classified under 'Intellectual Property', 'Distribution and Service Centre', or 'Headquarters' activities; the PIF must evidence a physical office in Panama, locally qualified employees, core income-generating activities (contract negotiation with Apple/Google, pricing, licensing, treasury management) executed in Panama, Council meeting minutes, and complete accounting records. Annual ESR filing is mandatory; failure to meet substance triggers fines of USD/PAB 1,000 to USD/PAB 25,000 per violation and, in repeated default, cancellation or dissolution of the entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Characterizing Panama-source in-app purchase revenue as entirely foreign-source, omitting Apple/Google payout reports on the Form 300, or failing to file the annual return for three consecutive fiscal years while operating the MMORPG from Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax crime under Ley 76 of 2019 and Fiscal Code Articles 738-745: surcharge of 10% per month (cap 100%), evaded-tax fines of 50%-200%, and imprisonment from 2 to 5 years where the evaded amount exceeds approximately USD/PAB 100,000; chronic non-filing results in entity strike-off.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Council members and the administrator are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of evaded taxes; the DGI may obtain preventive asset attachment and travel bans (prohibición de salida) against the Council president; criminal conviction carries imprisonment and disqualification from holding directorships.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Panama PIF holding global MMORPG IP and treasury while executing zero operational activity in Panama: no office, no staff, no Council minutes, and the central decisions are taken abroad; the entity is used as a letterbox to avoid gaming-platform source taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic Substance Rule violations: administrative fines of USD/PAB 1,000 to USD/PAB 25,000 per violation; the ESR authority may cancel the foundation's registration; foreign tax authorities may reclassify the PIF as a foreign tax resident, with ensuing back taxes, penalties, and denial of treaty benefits; loss of Article 723-A export-services shelter with full recomputation of tax at 25%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The public registry and courts pierce the foundation Council veil where the entity is a façade; directors are personally liable to the foundation's beneficiaries and third-party creditors for damages; repeated ESR non-compliance triggers a travel ban and disqualification from managing regulated entities.
